Reading

The innocent reading first, and it largely holds. At the alternative's name the Overview gives it at its own grain: its sequence, its originator and essay, its proponents by name, and its central argument in the archive's own terms, an account from extant texts that needs no lost one. It is the control against the Q addresses: the asymmetry the study names is stated plainly here, as the advocates' argument.

Findings
  • THE ARGUMENT FROM EXTANT TEXTS, STATED. 'Advocates point out that it simplifies literary history by relying only on existing, canonical gospels rather than postulating a lost document (Q).' The composition gives the distinction #1735's classes draw (extant antecedent and reconstructed antecedent) as this hypothesis's argument; at 'q source' and 'is the q source real' the same distinction does not enter the account of Q's evidence.
  • STANDING FROM A FORUM. 'it remains a notable minority view rather than the majority consensus in mainstream New Testament scholarship', 'As discussed on Reddit's AcademicBiblical community'. The minority standing of the hypothesis that dispenses with the unattested document is warranted by a forum thread, as the critical edition's standing is at 'critical edition of q'.
  • WHAT IS ACCURATE. Farrer 1955, 'On Dispensing with Q'; Goulder and Goodacre; the sequence; the standard objection (the dismantling of the Sermon on the Mount).
  • SMALLEST REPAIR. None needed for accuracy; the standing could be cited to the field's surveys. COUNTERTEST: none; the address serves as the control for the Q addresses.

The numbered citation links are Google redirects, kept in the raw transcript; the source cards listed in the cite list as pasted.] [QUERENT] farrer hypothesis [SYSTEM] The Farrer hypothesis is a proposed solution to the [synoptic problem](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHEIkXXmTGPkfvDlHEO1eoiKqEno3AV_JhHgXiSe6w7u8aurltvB7t3v2d_Ib5GWoqoEpL_LQ3xoOX66bMaoNIJP5fhPR9OM_2MDs-qAd09n2BwZZUq3ZVphE8oUYJP-FG9T8AZKoXx0JsvTg) in biblical studies that eliminates the need for the hypothetical "Q" document. [1] Core Literary Sequence The theory proposes the following order of composition: 1. Gospel of Mark was written first. 2. Gospel of Matthew was written second, using Mark as a primary source. 3. Gospel of Luke was written third, using both Mark and Matthew as sources. [1] Key Details and Origin * Originator: Proposed in 1955 by English biblical scholar Austin Farrer in his essay "On Dispensing with Q". [1] * Proponents: Developed and championed by later scholars including Michael Goulder and Mark Goodacre. [1] * Alternative Names: Also known as the Farrer–Goulder hypothesis or the Farrer–Goulder–Goodacre hypothesis. [1] * Major Contrast: It stands as a direct alternative to the dominant Two-Source Hypothesis (which posits that Matthew and Luke independently used Mark and a lost collection of sayings known as Q). [[1], [2]] Arguments For and Against * Arguments For: Advocates point out that it simplifies literary history by relying only on existing, canonical gospels rather than postulating a lost document (Q). It also provides a straightforward explanation for the "double tradition" (material shared by Matthew and Luke but absent in Mark), suggesting Luke simply integrated and adapted Matthew's material alongside Mark. [[1], [2]] * Arguments Against: Critics argue that the theory requires Luke to systematically dismantle, rearrange, and recontextualize Matthew's well-organized discourses (such as breaking up the Sermon on the Mount) in ways that seem complex or counterintuitive for an ancient author. As discussed on [Reddit's AcademicBiblical community](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF1zcUui1rDNS_qyEHw69R6w2wU4fnZS5ovSsuK-Sg0NovhEUoeWNdCTuPEBNk_5ua6GpRq4Ou6Y2nqmEHGQLkpMXY5tgT1QeLgO09JfRVwFV08hOby1YPtyioCuX26LDa-1f4RhJx14Sg7axw2RkgkJKd0LgzttwyMqMcZTUeH-U60hyinXY), it remains a notable minority view rather than the majority consensus in mainstream New Testament scholarship.
